decision: Treat priority 22 as one server-authoritative transaction spanning quote, reservation, execution outcome, and settlement
why: The roadmap requires failures to consume or refund the same committed resources consistently across every casting medium

decision: Keep casting method separate from persisted spell medium and add engraving as the fourth artifact medium
why: Bare and ritual casts have no artifact while scroll, book, engraving, and installed circle retain different lifecycles

decision: Use four vanilla items as the first reagent set
why: Amethyst shard, sugar, glowstone dust, and fermented spider eye already communicate the four effects and avoid adding placeholder item art before priority 28 balance and art passes

decision: Put one CastingResourceService reservation around both compatibility SpellEngine casts and delayed vm2 casts
why: The same quote and outcome matrix must govern authored circles, library spells, media, and automation without trusting client state

decision: Reserve a scroll stack before execution, consume it on success or genuine fault, refund it for infrastructure and lifecycle outcomes, and update reusable media only after success
why: This makes single-use loss atomic while preserving reusable books and installed artifacts

decision: Refund active reservations directly from logout, clone, dimension-change, and shutdown hooks before VM records are removed
why: An owner may be absent from the server player list by the next tick, so tick-only cleanup cannot guarantee exact inventory and mana restoration

decision: Do not close priority 22 after the first green ladder
why: Read-only review found silent unloaded-target success, offline/shutdown escrow loss, offering/reagent conflation, opaque clipping text, and insufficient GameTest reachability
result: all blocking findings resolved before closeout

decision: Use Nether Quartz as a separately staged offering-only pool
why: A ritual offering is a commitment requirement, not a fifth discount or a duplicate use of a typed reagent
evidence: CastingResourceService staging document vr-reagents:2; Field Manual v9

decision: Retain the exact payer object for each process-local reservation and settle active reservations without consulting the connected-player list
why: Logout races and shutdown can remove the owner lookup before exact inventory and mana restoration
result: absent-owner and shutdown fallback GameTests passed

decision: Track terminal callback delivery on each active VM
why: Lifecycle signals may repeat even though resource settlement is idempotent; media callbacks must also run at most once

decision: Classify missing direct VM entities and required semantic targets as UNLOADED_TARGET and protected effects as POLICY_REJECTED
why: Infrastructure/policy loss must refund rather than masquerade as success or a genuine player-authored spell fault

decision: Show both requested and applied discount amounts and name cap/floor clipping
why: Players need to audit how server floors and caps altered staged reagent contributions
result: requested 5.00, applied 5.00, quartz no-discount text observed

decision: Run the final build, GameTests, client, and visual closeout only on Hermes
why: Ian explicitly prohibited further NixOS execution after the earlier local launcher was closed
result: instruction honored; both Hermes units inactive and port 25575 free

decision: Require all six media reservation paths, separate offering semantics, consuming and refundable outcomes, absent-owner/shutdown fallback, unloaded target, and duplicate lifecycle coverage
why: A class or stub is insufficient for a checked roadmap item
evidence: 254 JUnit tests; 23 production GameTests; verify-priority22; Hermes checkpoint
result: accepted as coherent end-to-end alpha pass

decision: Run the global shutdown-refund GameTest in its own batch and assert per-owner escrow counts
why: The first final rerun exposed cross-test interference because refundAll and global activeCount shared state with concurrently running GameTests
evidence: Priority22GameTests priority22_escrow_isolated batch; two consecutive full GameTest runs

decision: Make Hermes the default for builds, tests, Minecraft, screenshots, and visual inspection; require Ian's approval before any NixOS execution or opening
why: Ian repeated this boundary and asked that future AIs inherit it
evidence: AGENTS.md; scripts/README.md; scripts/check-handoff-docs.sh; Vector-Regnum vault notes
result: documented with an executable stale-handoff guard

decision: Record and clean up an accidental NixOS launcher invocation caused by local shell interpretation of Markdown backticks
why: The invocation violated Ian's machine boundary and must remain visible to future reviewers
evidence: vector-regnum-local-server.service; runClient PIDs 42255 and 42539; loopback port 25575
result: local server and both client processes stopped; service inactive; port free; subsequent edits performed through quoted Hermes-only commands

decision: Keep remote mutations inside a single quoted SSH operation
why: A remote heredoc was followed by a local chmod attempt; it failed because the target file did not exist on NixOS and changed nothing
evidence: shell error; canonical checkout target absent
result: switched to one SSH mutation per tool call and created the checker only on Hermes

decision: Add and run a Hermes-only public-clone overlay checker
why: The guarded mirror has no Git metadata, so future agents need a rerunnable whitespace and new-file check
result: the first run found three generated .orig backups; exact backups removed; rerun printed HERMES_DIFF_CHECK_OK
